scope: Static answer-menu factorial with identical literal question/full state; no driving claim or preset promotion.

factorial_effects.scope: Descriptive matched differences; neither independent-sample significance nor an internal causal mechanism is identified.

limitations: Twenty-four fresh synthetic geometries in twelve mirrored pairs and repeated conditions are not independent driving trials.

Meaningful versus opaque ID strings change semantic content, tokenization and string length together. Physical versus numeric descriptions also change wording and length; no specific internal bias mechanism is established.
The literal question and full named observation remain physical in all contexts. Numeric criterion descriptions do not neutralize the entire task framing.
Physical angle insertion order is matched across conditions and nearly counterbalanced across units. Submitted wire order does not prove the provider exposes that order internally.
Repeated requests can use different opaque ID-to-angle assignments and insertion orders; repeat agreement compares physical angles, not answer-ID strings.
No worked examples or current-query arithmetic are supplied. Coarse wheel answers cannot prove exact trigonometry, optimal driving or closed-loop reliability.
Heading-sign mismatch groups can differ in target magnitude; subgroup scores do not isolate a sign-conflict effect.
Endpoint errors count as incorrect in attempted accuracy; planned coverage and unrun cases remain separate.
recommendation: Retain damped as live baseline and original application default. Combined opaque IDs and numeric descriptions improve full-left answers but regress moderate steering; all candidates fail the overall,per-magnitude and gain gates. No further paid validation or promotion.

audited_factorial_effects.scope: Descriptive matched differences; neither independent-sample significance nor an internal causal mechanism is identified.

interpretation: The combined opaque-ID/numeric-description menu scores 40/48 versus 37/48 for semantic IDs with physical descriptions. Its gain is only 3/48 (6.25 percentage points); 83.3% overall, 13/16 full and 11/16 moderate all miss the declared quality or gain thresholds. No candidate triggers follow-up.

Combined versus control yields seven gains and four losses. Gains are five full-left, one full-right and one straight answer. Losses are three moderate-right and one moderate-left answer; each new error selects full rather than moderate with the correct sign. Full-target accuracy rises 7/16 to 13/16 while moderate accuracy falls 15/16 to 11/16.

Combined chosen full wheels rise from eight to eighteen: correct full answers rise from seven to thirteen, while wrong full-for-moderate answers rise from one to five. All five combined moderate-target misses select a full wheel. This is a magnitude tradeoff, not general faithful execution of the formula.

ID changes depend on description context. Opaque IDs with physical descriptions score one fewer correct answer than semantic IDs (two gains, three losses); opaque IDs with numeric descriptions score six more (ten gains, four losses). The matched difference of these effects is 7/48, or 14.58 percentage points. The descriptive mean ID effect is 5.21 points and mean description effect 1.04 points; these averages hide the interaction.

Every nonzero answer in every condition follows raw-y sign. Correct direction does not establish correct magnitude, arithmetic or optimal control. The menu package changes string semantics, length and tokenization together; observed differences do not identify an internal bias mechanism.

The second presentation of each case changes physical insertion order; opaque conditions also change ID-to-angle mapping. Physical angles match on 21/24, 22/24, 22/24 and 20/24 cases for the four contexts respectively. Raw opaque IDs match only 2/24 in either opaque condition. These are changed-presentation comparisons, not identical-request repeatability tests.

No condition repeats the chosen submitted insertion position on any case pair. This is inconsistent with a universal fixed submitted-position strategy on these cases. The provider may reorder or encode criteria internally; submitted wire order does not identify its internal presentation or establish a causal position effect.

The eight x=15-discriminating answers score 5/8, 4/8, 5/8 and 4/8 across the four contexts. Combined accuracy improves only on the other fixtures (36/40 versus 32/40), providing no gain on this particular actual-x discrimination test. Matching a shortcut label alone does not identify internal x substitution.

Mirrored cases, two presentations, four menu conditions and multiple paired contrasts are correlated. Counts and matched effects are descriptive; the combined menu has not qualified a reliable live driver.
